_what: Synthetic Dart accessor-scope and parameter-redeclaration gate for #3904 (DART-10, stacked on #3903 / DART-11), following bench/ruby-gem-resolution and bench/dart-deferred-imports: exact accuracy cells and fingerprints, with ratios as the only timing gates. Real capture emitter, real parse worker (dist/), real Dart ScopeResolver and pubspec loader; analyze, persistence and full-pipeline memory are outside this benchmark.
_triage: Shape and fingerprint failures are deterministic: inspect the corpus and the resolved edges, never rebaseline just to make CI green. The runner also fails, before any baseline comparison, when a class or function misses an expected method CALLS edge or gains one the source never makes. For a timing failure, rerun on an idle machine and verify the report shows its profile (ci: 5 interleaved samples after 1 warmup; full: 15 after 2) before investigating a regression. Millisecond observations are context, not gates.
_shape_note: Exact counts are the workload FLOOR. small = 64 units x 4, large = 256 x 4 (classes or functions 4x), dense = 64 x 16 (accessors per class or parameters per function 4x). Expected method edges per unit are computed from the source, not read back from the graph: each getter's local types `v.save()` as Address.save, each setter's `Other value` types `value.run()` as Other.run, `reader()` reads the untyped field and gets nothing; each `a<j>.run()` reaches Address.run because only the closure redeclares `a<j>`. On #3903's head the accessor form misses every setter edge and gains a wrong `reader -> Address.save` per class (32 missing and 16 wrong at 16 x 4), so this gate fails without #3904; the params form is identical there and measures the per-scope redeclaration count's cost.
_fingerprint_note: Hashes pin every relationship (endpoints, type, confidence, reason) and every decline (reason/detail, file, name, position).
_scaling_note: Scaling ratios are (t_4n/t_n)/4: about 1 is linear, about 4 is quadratic. 1.5 (bench/scope-capture) on every ratio but one. accessors_resolve_unit_scaling_ratio keeps 2.2 (bench/ruby-gem-resolution): resolution is already super-linear in the number of classes in one file on #3903's head, the base this stacks on (fitted exponent 1.55 (1.43-1.67) over 128 -> 2048 classes, against 1.42 (1.34-1.51) with #3904).
_profiles_note: Two profiles share the shapes and every accuracy gate. CI (the default, and what --check runs in the benchmarks job): one process, one parse worker, every workload timed, min of 5 after 1 warmup, interleaved. --full: one child times every workload, min of 15 after 2 warmups, and each shape runs in a fresh child for its peak RSS. Wall times are in _measured_ci.
_negative_controls_note: Re-walking the scope body for every parameter binding in dartParameterRedeclared (O(parameters x body), a temporary edit of languages/dart/captures.ts) fails params_capture_per_unit_scaling_ratio 1.872 > 1.5 in the CI profile (1.810 under the full protocol at the earlier 128/512 shapes), with unchanged fingerprints. This is a deliberate regression, not a baseline observation.

_measured_ci.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_full.environment: macOS arm64 / Node 24.16.0, 2026-11-13, shared host (load average 7-40 on 15 cores)

_measured_note: Three CI-profile runs and one --full run at 2afddfce1. Scalar ratios and millisecond values are per-metric maxima across the runs of that profile (rounded). peak_rss_mib (--full only) is each --shape child's high-water mark after one worker parse and one resolution, worker thread included; context, not gated. Exact shapes and fingerprints were identical in all runs. The doubling sweep in the PR comment (128 -> 2048 units and 4 -> 64 per unit, three rounds, #3903's head 82c585d89 and #3904's head 2afddfce1) was measured separately with --shape --reps 3 --warmup 1 and is part of neither profile.
